title: Contextual sticky column rail with compact sparkline previews
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our virtualized table is increasingly used for dense operational dashboards. Users need quick, glanceable signals per column (trend, sort state, active filters) without paying the hit of full DOM expansion or breaking virtualization. Current header affordances are either too heavy (full filter/sort menus) or invisible for dense modes.

Goal: Introduce a lightweight, virtualization-friendly 'sticky column rail' that appears when hovering or when a column is pinned. The rail hosts compact controls (sort toggle, quick filter badge, and a 24px sparkline) that are rendered with canvas/SVG fallbacks and only mount when visible to preserve scroll performance. The feature should work across density modes (compact, comfortable), support keyboard and touch, and expose state to the Console for telemetry.

Proposed solution summary:
- Column rail: a 28px-wide overlay anchored to the column edge (left or right depending on text direction) that becomes 'sticky' while a column is pinned or during a drag interaction. Should not affect layout width to preserve virtualized measurements.
- Compact sparkline: 24x18px edible preview showing recent distribution/metric for that column. Render as lightweight SVG layer with a rasterized canvas fallback when the column list is > 200 to avoid token pressure. Sparklines use a DT-based color token and respect high-contrast mode.
- Progressive mount: Controls (sparkline, sort, filter chip) are not in the DOM until hover/focus or when the column is actively pinned/dragged. Use IntersectionObserver/hover intent (150ms) to avoid churn on quick mouse passes.
- Density compatibility: In 'compact' table density the rail overlays cell gutters; in 'comfortable' mode it uses a slightly larger hover target. In collapsed/stacked mobile fallbacks the rail collapses into a single overflow button that opens the full column menu.
- Accessibility: Keyboard focus target order must include the rail controls. Provide aria-live summaries for filter changes and keyboard hints for sparkline expansion. Ensure 4.5:1 contrast for icons in normal mode and 3:1 in high-contrast options if necessary with an accessible toggle.
- Metrics and observability: Emit events when users open the rail, toggle sort via rail, and expand sparkline. Measure mount cost (ms) and reflow occurrences to validate performance targets.

Trade-offs considered:
- Full-time rendering of sparklines is simpler but would degrade virtualization performance; we prefer on-demand mount.
- Using a CSS-only solution would be lighter but cannot reliably provide canvas fallbacks and precise pixel rendering for sparklines.
- Mount-on-hover with long hover intent reduces accidental mounts but can delay discoverability; mitigated by showing a subtle affordance (thin hairline) to indicate rail presence on hover.

Acceptance criteria (must pass for Done):
1) Rail appears on hover after 150ms and immediately when a column is pinned or during drag.
2) Sparkline renders under 6ms for visible columns and falls back to raster canvas when columns > 200 with no perceptible jank (<10ms extra frame).
3) All controls reachable by keyboard in source order and announced by screen readers (verify with VoiceOver and NVDA).
4) Density modes preserved: compact overlay and comfortable overlay visuals validated across breakpoints.
5) Telemetry events emitted for rail open, sort toggle, and sparkline expand.
6) Unit and visual regression tests added; perf regression budget defined and met.

Design artifacts and figma links are listed in attachments. Engineering notes: prefer a portal strategy to render rails outside the immediate virtualized cell container to avoid layout thrashing. Use a single shared canvas layer for multiple sparklines when possible to pool GPU work.

Next steps:
- Design: finalize tokens and states (Aisha) by 2026-03-16.
- Eng: spike for canvas-based sparklines and telemetry (ENG-2244) due 2026-03-20.
- PM: validate with two customers who maintain wide operational tables (PM-512) and gather feedback on discoverability.

Risks:
- Incorrect mounting heuristics could still cause reflow; measure in staging with large tables (>10k rows).
- Accessibility edge cases around screen readers announcing dynamically added content; require ARIA review.

Notes: This ticket intentionally keeps the full filter menu out of the rail to avoid conflating responsibilities — the rail is for quick actions and glanceable previews only.
